pool.text: Frederick Schwatka observed the presence of a portage trail used to bypass Miles Canyon.
The discovery of gold in the Klondike set off a major regional change.
Construction finished the difficult Bennett Lake section, completing the entire railway route.
The first White Horse General Hospital was built in the downtown area.
Residents of the Yukon have been voting federally since a byelection.
A small fire in the Windsor Hotel barber shop got out of control.
The very first air mail was successfully sent to the community.
The US military began construction of the Alaska Highway to transfer troops.
The city was officially incorporated in this notable historical year.
The city was designated the capital of the Yukon Territory.
The name was officially changed from White Horse to Whitehorse.
The Yukon News was founded as a weekly publication by Ken Shortt.
CBC Television operated an affiliate named CFWH-TV in the area.
The Metropolitan Whitehorse development plan included preserved park and greenbelt areas.
Whitehorse Bylaw restricts motor vehicles to designated roadways in Protected Areas.
A French-language newspaper named L'Aurore boreale was founded.
A wartime-era hangar was replaced with a modern terminal building.
The Yukon Hospital Corporation was created to prepare the transfer of powers.
The city approved the Area Development Scheme for Whitehorse Copper.
Yukon's electoral map was modified to give Whitehorse an extra seat.
